messages.subject: Re: [RRO] Cant install Bioconductor with Revolution R Open 8.0.1 beta3
messages.subject_clean: [RRO] Cant install Bioconductor with Revolution R Open 8.0.1 beta3
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stephen,
Please add a `repositories` file to your RRO install. We are still investigating why RRO for Ubuntu is not putting this file in the right place. We have a bug report for this in the works.

As a one-off work around for now please do the following in your Ubuntu installation:

As user root create this file with your text editor or using wget:

cd /usr/lib64/RRO-8.0.2/R-3.1.2/lib/R/etc/
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RRO/master/R-src/etc/repositories
R
source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite()

Thank you,
Chris Mosetick

messages.subject: Error on running RevoScaleR Demo - Airline table
messages.subject_clean: Error on running RevoScaleR Demo - Airline table
messages.body_plain:
Hello ,

  I was taking R code straight from R revolutionary example; and tried to run it but it gave me error complaining that it could not find  function "RxOdbcData". I have no idea of what went gone; so I seek your help in this forum to show me what I missed.

Thanks so much. Below is the R code.

#####################################################
#####################################################
##
## RevoScaleR Demo - Airline table
##
## Hortonworks Sandbox Hadoop demo
## Using "Beside" Architecture
##
##
## all column names imported as lower case
##
#####################################################
#####################################################

#####################################################
##
## general definitions
##
#####################################################

## filenames, location, etc.
OdbcConnString <- "DSN=Sample Hortonworks Hive DSN"

odbcDS <- RxOdbcData(sqlQuery = "SELECT * FROM airline",
                                connectionString=OdbcConnString,
                                stringsAsFactors=TRUE,
       useFastRead = TRUE,
       rowsPerRead=150000)

xdfFile <- "airlineHWS.xdf"

if(file.exists(xdfFile)) file.remove(xdfFile)
rxImportToXdf(odbcDS, xdfFile,overwrite=TRUE)

#####################################################
##
## Inspect the data
##
#####################################################

## get general information about the file and the variables in it
rxGetInfo(data=xdfFile, getVarInfo=TRUE,numRows=3)

## a summary of time and distance:
rxSummary(~arrdelay + depdelay + dayofweek, data=xdfFile)

## we can inspect them visually, too. A histogram of departure delays, for example:
rxHistogram(~depdelay, data=xdfFile)

## can use parameters similar to a regular histogram to zero in on the interesting area
rxHistogram(~depdelay, data=xdfFile, xAxisMinMax=c(50, 200), numBreaks=500,xNumTicks=10)

#####################################################
##
## Analytics!
##
## Run a regression:
##
#####################################################

## before you run a regression, run a correlation
rxCor(formula=~depdelay+arrdelay, data=xdfFile)

##  a linear regression:
system.time(reg1 <- rxLinMod(formula=arrdelay~depdelay, data=xdfFile,rowSelection=(arrdelay>0) & (arrdelay <800)))

summary(reg1)
#############################################

## a generalized linear model:
system.time(glm1 <- rxGlm(formula=arrdelay~depdelay, data=xdfFile))

Hi All,

I was wondering whether I can select a different local snapshot directory other than the default ~/.checkpoint/.

I find the ~/.checkpoint/DATE structure to be very useful mainly because it avoids creating a package directory for every project. BUT pointing to a different path other than the default one is useful for a variety of reasons. In my case I'm using R from a portable USB pendrive but ~/. is poiting to the usual Document folder in the local C drive which is creating duplicates when I plug my pen into different computers rather than having a unique ~/.checkpoint/DATE directory on my portable pen.

Thanks for any hints,
Paolo

messages.subject: Changing the column positions of an xdf dataset
messages.subject_clean: Changing the column positions of an xdf dataset
messages.body_plain:
I would like to know if there is a way to reorder the column positions of an xdf dataset. For example, if I have an xdf dataset with columns [,a],[,c],[,b], I would like to reorder the columns to [,a],[,b],[,c] without having to create a dataframe, reorder the columns, and use RxImport or rxDataFrameToXdf to convert it back to an xdf file (because the xdf file potentially has 100s of millions of rows and I don't want to write the dataset to memory).

One potential solution I see is using the rxSetVarInfoXdf function, which has information on the column position.
Something like:
#Swap positions for columns 2 and 3
varInfo <- list(list(position = 2, position = 3), list(position = 3, position = 2))

But this will not work as position is a value which you call to reference the column but not to change it.
